column2: The Soviets have slipped south into Greece and Turkey.  A large naval task force has been spotted in your region.  Find a suitable landing area quickly and get the Soviets the Hell out of Helles!
Playing Tip #1: Use Air Recon to spot ships near coast
Playing Tip #2: Deployed ships can be easy targets for long range enemy firepower.  Do not over deploy.
Playing Tip #3: The Soviets are very aggressive.  Get on the beach and prepare for an attack using defensive air cover.
Ari Burnu - May 3rd, 1946
The Soviets have set up defensive position in the mountains.  You must find a way through the mountains, escarpments, and minefields to rid Turkey of the Soviet occupation.
The initial landing area has proven to be inhospitable.  Scout the region for a better landing area.
That was unacceptable.
Your performance makes me wonder if you're the right guy for the job.
Korinth - June 26th, 1946

Three major naval ports have been mined; battleships have been spotted in two ports and submarines in the third.  Be careful when approaching these ports because we suspect the enemy can fire upon us even when docked.
You must find a landing area quickly before the Soviet naval forces break free of the mines.
Commander, you have taken too long to succeed. We cannot afford to keep taking such losses. We expect much more from you.
Crete - July 26th, 1946

The Soviet air force has retreated back home to Russia.  Our blockade of the Black Sea has kept the Soviet Navy in local waters.  You must make your landing immediately before they have a chance to stop us.
With nowhere else to run, expect entrenched elite troops to fight to the last man.
Splendid job, Commander! The missiles are neutralized, and our forces can
push farther into Russia now that the threat of Armageddon no longer hangs
over our heads...
Gibraltar - September 30th, 1946

The British are in control of Gibraltar and are receiving support from the best that the Americans and Soviets can offer.  We have mined their naval port but this is not expected to keep them out of the battle for too long.
We have sent elements from the Atlantic fleet as reinforcements; they will arrive shortly.  Our missile batteries are being installed but we suggest you do not wait and commence the final assault.
Seal the Mediterranean and return home a hero.
Playing Tip #1: Missiles love to shoot at Recon.
Playing Tip #2: Sometimes it better to wait for the enemy to come to you.
Comrade General your failure to break the lines on the flanks of Sixth Army has meant that the enemy still threatens Stalingad! Vassiliev is very upset with your incompetence!
Malta - September 9th, 1945
Commander, the British Navy is fast approaching to aid the already entrenched defenses.  You must find and destroy the British Navy or the planned landing will not succeed.
Expect well bunkered artillery and a strong air defense.  Intelligence reports no enemy submarine activity.
Do not fail us.

Commander, that was outstanding! You have managed to hold the russians back and even push them back past their jump off point. Now we need you to continue to hold the line. The Reds have us pinned in an area south of here and we could be in big trouble if they manage to push through. You must stop them!
The enemy has been unable to crack our new Funkschlüssel and is spread thin across thousands of kilometers of coastal territory.  The time is right to invade British occupied Algeria.
Algiers - October 10th, 1945
Commander, the British have been demoralized but their erroneous belief that they are masters in desert warfare keeps their spirit alive.  You must crush them!
Advance Fallschirmjager scouts report just a small French detachment.  It appears our deception of landing in Tunisia has succeeded and the British have left Algiers unguarded.
Tunis - November 2nd, 1945
We have pushed the British out of Algeria and now the time has come to liberate Tunisia from Churchill's tyranny.

Expect a strong defensive stand from the British with little naval support.  Be cautious of exposing your fleet to enemy artillery.  Also, there are rumors of a British submarine design that is difficult to detect.
Playing Tip #1: Capture the port at Bizerte to deploy naval units.
Playing Tip #2: Do not run out of ammo in the sand.

General, the White House and Pentagon is ours. The cradle of Capitalism has collapsed. Stalin is delighted and proud of you because you allowed him to be in a very strong position at the peace negotiation table. Remnants of US army must now surrender and the US communist party can rule the country according to Moscow's wills.

You and your troops have freed Leningrad.  The birthplace of the revolution can again breathe the sweet air of freedom.  Now, we must help our Finnish brothers to the north to escape the fascist scourge. That will be all, Comrade General.
Medenine - November 21st, 1945
Commander, Welcome to Phase II of the operation to free Tunisia.

The remnants of the British army have retreated south to fortified positions in the hills.  With no place left to run, expect massive amounts of troops to surrender.  It is believed that the enemy navy is operating out of the numerous ports in the region.
As you near the Soviet controlled Libyan border there will be a large show of Russian military might.  It is just a show.  Diplomatic negotiations will keep the Russians out of this fight.
Playing Tip #1: Capture the port at Gabes to deploy naval units.
The Soviets attempt to surround the new German Sixth Army at Cherkassy in the  Ukraine.
Tripoli - December 7th, 1945
Commander, your leadership is now needed to free Libya.

The Soviets are in control of Libya and they are ready to repel our offensive.  You must act quickly before they can entrench themselves.  A naval port is required to bring in reinforcements from Tunisia.
Playing Tip: Capture the port at Tripoli.
The city remains in Soviet hands, blockading the northern roads to Moscow.
Now our forces will be forced to head directly into the gauntlet in front of the Soviet capital, costing us men, time and maybe even the war... You are dismissed.
Agedabia - December 23rd, 1945

Intelligence reports that an entire Russian Armored Corp and several independant Tank Brigades are bearing down on the coast as we speak. You need to hit the beach ASAP so that your Naval support can defend against an expected heavy Soviet surface ship counterattack.
Do not underestimate the enemy defenses.
Comrade General you have achieved complete victory! The German are retreating towards the Dnepr river at full speed! We have them on the run!
Tobruk - January 7th, 1946
Commander, the initial amphibious landing has stalled.  You must get on the beach and find a way to break through the enemy defenses.

Tobruk is heavily defended and is meant to be a distraction to consume all our resources while the enemy escapes into Egypt via Sidi Rezegi.  Captured German equipment has been reported being used by the enemy.
Remove the Russian scourge from the African continent forever.
Sevastopol-Kersones
Vacha
Sidi Barrani - January 21st, 1946
Commander, the American forces that you defeated in Sicily have occupied Egypt.  You must liberate Egypt.

The American tanks are inferior to ours but their air power should not be underestimated.  Intelligence has reported a new American submarine that is deadly.  Fortunately only one of these submarines is expected in the area and should not cause any problems to our mighty Navy.
Longest path: 18
Campaign designer: Lester Hathaway 04/2010

Welcome to Mediterranean 46! This is a fictional campaign. The premise is simple; Germany has risen from the ashes! A leadership change has sparked the superior capability of the Wehrmacht to retake what was once theirs.  This campaign begins at the final stage of the Italian offensive and takes the German commander throughout the Mediterranean; establishing bases in preparation for future expansion of the German empire in Africa and the Middle East.

The Kriegsmarine is providing a large Task Force throughout this campaign to get rid the Mediterranean of American, British, and Soviet occupation.  There exists no current capability to overstrength or replace Naval units during the campaign.  Damaged units will be restored to their original strength at the start of each scenario.
This campaign was designed for experts and is not for the faint at heart. Use of Bat Wing fighters and bombers are not recommended.
Equipment File: European E-File
PG2 Campaign Designer: Technique, 01/2008
PeG-WW2 conversion: Robert Mary, 08/2008

The Leibstandarte began its life as the 'SS-Stabswache Berlin', acting as bodyguards for the Nazi leader Adolf Hitler.  It was the first armed SS formation and, by most measures, the most capable.  Initially they were referred to contemptuously by the Heer regulars as the 'asphalt soldiers' for their obsessive spit and polish drill and purely ceremonial duties.  After the campaigns in Poland and France, contempt gave way to geniune respect as the Leibstandarte earned a reputation as a combat unit which lived for the 'sheer beauty of the fighting'.
Other campaigns at http://www.pegww2.net
Amiens - January 5th, 1946
The advance through France continue successfully, like in Italy.
This time, your mission will be to capture the city of Amiens.
Soon continental Europe will be ours.
All right, Commander, a job well done!  The Krauts never knew what hit them.  Well, we're really looking good, thanks to you.  Hey, rumor has it the president may want to pin a medal on you himself.
I had hoped for a deeper penetration General.
However, you've gotten Ivan's attention and he will have to slow his
advance against the British.
Hypothetical German-Italian invasion of the British controlled island of
Malta.
Sitting astride the sea lanes between Italy and Libya, the British-held
island of Malta proved a major nuisance to Italian efforts to push supply
convoys across the Mediterranean Sea.  The German plan (Operation
Hercules) put its faith in airborne landings.  German and Italian
paratroopers would secure the most important points, and reinforcements
would then come over the beaches to finish off the island's garrison.
This is one of the game's smallest maps, and provides a naval conflict as
part of the action.
The Germans have pushed us back to our starting point. We will be lucky if we can halt them.  Your brave men have suffered terribly. You are ordered back to London where you will face a firing squad!
That was as fine an example of mobile warfare as I've ever seen.
They'll be using this one at the armor school for quite a few years.
The Poles are clamoring to throw a big bash for their liberator, enjoy
yourself.
Gibraltar or Bust
September 20, 1940

After the fall of France, the Axis powers look for an avenue to Gibraltar.  They ask their one time partner, the Spanish Nationalists, but they deny land passage to the Straits.  With backing from the British, the Spanish await the Axis onslaught.
16 Air Army Air Field

Well, you really dropped the ball this time.  It was crucial...critical to get past Metz and move into Germany.  Instead, we're still bogged down.  There's no time for fooling around; we're going to have to go this thing all over again.  But this time, with another  guy in charge.  I'm sending you stateside, Commander.

Good day, Commander.  British troops are to land at Salerno with the assistance of sundry American formations.   Be advised to press on from the beachhead as quickly as possible since recent reports indicate the presence of a panzer division hiding in the area.  Then, it is imperative, Commander, to drive on.  This will secure our line of supply as we continue our drive North.
The Germans attack the American and French forces near Strassbourg.
General, our advance along the railroad is going nicely.
Ivan isn't happy and has pooled most of his forces in the Far East to stop
us.
G2 reports two whole fronts on the move towards Khabarovsk.
If we can get their first, we'll cut their supply lines.
Drive like hell general, time is of the essence.
USSAF
This is absolutely unacceptable. Now all we have to do is wait for the first missiles to crash down upon western Europe...
Splendid job out there, Commander. Now it's time to interrogate the scientist and find those missiles, before it's too late.
Sicily
The Soviets go on the attack against the Germans in what was to become the largest tank battle in the world.
Comrade General you have failed to destroy the Italian Eighth Army! The Germans still threaten to release Sixth Army! Vassiliev is very disatisfied!
St. Lo - Advance on St. Lo: Redux
American forces strike the Germans near St. Lo in preparation for a full-
scale breakout.
Well Comrade, most of the fascist invaders are trapped.  At least, you accomplished your mission.  Now, you must prepare yourself for further operations.
Victory!, we have destroyed the British defensive lines with our Panzer Divisions, all the goals have been captured, the supply lines restored... and now, to London!.
The Soviets go on the attack against the Germans in what was to
become the largest tank battle in the world.
Excellent job General!
That terrain was brutal but you wern't slowed down a bit. I smell a promotion coming your way.
That was brilliant!
Commander that was a tough nut to crack but you pulled it off with great skill. Now on to Minsk.
Advanced Elements - October 11th, 1940
Excellent! your actions were better than we had expected, you will receive much prestige to reclaim some transport to your units plus any upgrade you may do.

An alternate history where Hitler was assassinated in 1935. With no
Nazi Germany to check his expansion in the east, Stalin invades Europe. Lead the Allied resistance to victory.
Your performance was barely adequate Commander. I expect more from you in the future.
Comrade General you have an opportunity to rehabilitate yourself! Marshall Zhukov wants you to reduce Budapest and hold off the German attacks in the Hungarian plains!
Nuclear Escalation (Part 2) - December 13th, 1941
Comrade, it was an expected defeat, but I want to ask you that don't give up and get back with the large amount of equipment as possible to build a more solid defense.
Nuclear Escalation (Part 1) - December 13th, 1941
General, you have made the impossible!, Stalin is glad with you and angry with the Americans, so he wants to invade America.
Comrade General your success has cleared this part of the Rodina from Germans invaders! STAVKA is very pleased with your command of the operation!
Sailboats on the Volga (Part 2) - February 13th, 1942
Comrade General you have resisted all German attacks! The city is solidly in our hands. We can look with confidence into the future!
Great work! The city has been liberated, and our forces continue to drive
farther inland, into the heart of the U.S.S.R...
Sailboats on the Volga (Part 1) - February 13th, 1942

Good day, Commander. It is your mission to capture the experimental Airbase at Dessau before the Soviets can get there.  Jerry's jet and rocket aircraft must not be allowed to fall into the wrong hands.  Good luck Commander, and God's speed.
The city is ours. However, the Germans are not impressed with the length of
the battle and the amount of casualties taken on both sides. Try not to
underwhelm our allies.
Great job, Commander! The attack into the Soviet homeland continues,
without fear of any super tanks halting our assault...
Ace in the Hole - April 19th, 1942

The Soviets have become extremely desperate in light of recent Allied success in capturing and holding Volgorad. Intelligence reports that the Soviets have begun testing of a super-heavy tank, which if produced in time for the assault on Moscow could easily turn the tide of the war. This must not happen.

Commander, you must take your forces and converge with nearby Allied troops in the area to take the weapons facility and destroy that tank. If we aren't quick enough, the blueprints will almost certainly be transmitted to another Soviet base. Take it out quickly and efficently, Commander. Good luck!

No doubt with the brutal attack on their base, the Soviets have already taken precautions for another attack and have transmitted the schematics to another base that we don't know about. Consider yourself dismissed.

Comrade General you failed to achieve a great success! You were able to secure a big beachhead on the right bank of the Dnepr river, but your slow attack allowed them to contain your position. You have to do better than that!
Good job, Commander! The gas has been neutralized. The men that served
under you have reported you to be quite likable as well.
Great job, Commander!  You have done an absolutely fantastic job with the
Sarin gas crisis. The men that served under you have nothing but praise for
your command skills.
Adrenaline Rush - May 10th, 1942
The attack on Moscow is in its preparation stages. Your forces are being positioned around the city itself along with the majority of Allied forces.

However, an extremely desperate plan by the Soviets to produce deadly Sarin nerve gas and drop it into the city upon Allied troops during the final thrust has shown itself.  The situation has risen to crisis-level as the Soviets prepare to ship the Sarin gas into trucks from a large manufacturing facility north-east of Moscow itself.  Unfortunately, we don't have the time to manoeuvre your forces to the crisis point, so you will have to use a highly trained force which has responded to the area.  Take the gas and prevent them from shipping it out.
You must hurry, so move quickly. Armored corps are on the way.
Good luck Commander, you will need it!!!

No doubt with the brutal attack on their base, the Soviets have already taken precautions for another attack and have transported the gas to another base that we don't know about. Consider yourself dismissed.
Comrade General you have stopped the Germans completely! Ponyri Station is safe! Vassiliev is very pleased with your performance!
Comrade General you have failed completely to destroy the Italian Eighth Army! The Germans are in condition to release Sixth Army! Vassiliev is very disatisfied!
Excellent. Once again the Americans owe you a debt of gratitude. It is rumored that they have suggested you for a medal of honor!
The Great War
A summary of the conflict from 1940-1942
(The following excerpt has been taken from The Great War, a definitive
summary of the conflict that engulfed Europe from 1940-1942.  We are most
grateful that the author has allowed us to take an excerpt from his book.)
Though they had nearly been crushed into the snow of the Russian winter, the
Allies had pushed the Soviets back from the borders of Germany all the way
into Moscow.  The Germans, French and British, united in their common goal,
attempted to enclose Moscow into a pocket from which no supplies could
reach the city. However, the Soviets crushed Erwin Rommel's German Army
Group B, and the French quickly retreated.  Only the British forces remained
intact and ready for battle.  The British taskforce, although severely
outnumbered, was able to take the Kremlin and the rest of the city and bring
the war to a close. Many Soviet officials were tried and found guilty of war
